problems.title: The released repair routine ignores the requested order
problems.source_location: Section 3.6 and Figure 3, PDF p. 5; Table 1, PDF p. 7; Appendix G, Table 10, PDF p. 24.
claim: Paraphrase. Section 3.6 distinguishes sequential, high-to-low, low-to-high, and random repair orders. Figure 3 illustrates their different trajectories; the lower panel of Table 1 and Appendix G, Table 10 report different detection results for the order variants pp. 5, 7, 24. Their meaning requires the repaired token sequence to depend on the chosen order.

The matching implementation is auc_perplexity in dna_detectllm/metrics.py, lines 53–210. Its active order-selection block is at lines 79–87 and the repair loop begins at line 89. The conference supplement and the pinned GitHub copy have identical bytes for this file. compute_anomaly_level calls this routine with repair_order="h2l"; the default compute_score instead calls sum_perplexity.
analysis: The function computes/shuffles sorted_indices according to the requested order, but the active update loop iterates unchanged change_indices. Its returned trajectory is therefore independent of every accepted order string for fixed inputs. Distinct order-ablation results cannot be reproduced by changing this parameter alone in the supplied routine.

problems.title: The paper and code assign opposite directions to cross entropy
problems.source_location: Eq. (1), PDF pp. 3–4; Section 4.1, PDF p. 6 (model roles).
claim: Eq. (1), PDF pp. 3–4, places reference-model probabilities from \(M_1\) outside the logarithm and observer-model probabilities from \(M_2\) inside it. Section 4.1, PDF p. 6, assigns those roles to Falcon-7B-Instruct and Falcon-7B. Interpreting the omitted vocabulary sum charitably gives cross entropy \(H(P,Q)=-\sum_iP_i\log Q_i\); the finding does not count the omitted sum as an error.
analysis: The released helper receives observer then reference distributions and computes \(H(Q,P)\), while the numerator retains reference probabilities. Cross entropy is asymmetric: for \(P\ne Q\), those expressions need not agree and can rank detector scores differently. Reversing model names only inside the denominator does not restore the full stated role contract.

For example, \(P=(0.9,0.1)\), \(Q=(0.5,0.5)\) give \(H(P,Q)=\log 2\approx0.69315\), while \(H(Q,P)=-\tfrac12\log(0.09)\approx1.20397\). With the same reference numerator these are different scores. This is an arithmetic witness to the direction mismatch, not a benchmark rerun.

problems.title: Probability order does not universally determine repair-score order
claim: Paraphrase. Section 3.6 associates high observed-token probability with smaller repair changes and describes high-probability repairs first as producing a higher trajectory score p. 5. The preceding discussion uses typically, so this analysis distinguishes an empirical tendency from a universal implication. The latter is not valid under the stated definitions. The result below is a scope clarification, not a refutation of the empirical curves.
analysis: Take valid four-token distributions \((0.40,0.50,0.05,0.05)\) and \((0.30,0.31,0.20,0.19)\), observing the first token in each. Their repair log changes are \(\log(0.50/0.40)\approx0.22314\) and \(\log(0.31/0.30)\approx0.03279\), so the higher observed probability gives the larger change. A uniform observer holds the denominator fixed. This excludes a universal ordering but is compatible with the source’s explicit typical-behavior qualification and empirical curves; it is not counted as a current error.
result: No current error is established by the universal interpretation. The source explicitly qualifies the probability-order explanation as typical and presents repair-order behavior empirically. The counterexample limits a stronger universal claim that is not required by that qualified wording.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
problems.impact_rationale: The manuscript explicitly presents a typical behavior and empirical heuristic; a counterexample to an unclaimed universal ordering does not constitute a current paper error.
problems.existing_correction_status: No correction is required for the qualified statement; no author adoption is asserted.
